import io

# Prepare the data
csv_data = """brand,model_year,megapixels,max_iso,weight_grams,price_usd,sensor_type,has_video_4k,lens_mount,body_type

Fuji,2019,46.4,51200,1151,3596.41,APS-C,0,EF,Mirrorless

"""

df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(csv_data))

# Set a professional and modern plot style
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", font_scale=1.1)
plt.rcParams['font.family'] = 'sans-serif'
plt.rcParams['font.sans-serif'] = 'Arial'

# Create the figure and axes
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 9))

# Create a bubble chart encoding multiple variables

scatter = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='price_usd',
    y='megapixels',
    size='weight_grams',
    hue='brand',
    style='body_type',
    sizes=(300, 3000),  # Control the range of bubble sizes
    palette='viridis',
    alpha=0.8,
    edgecolor='black',
    linewidth=1.5,
    ax=ax
)

    ax.text(
        row['price_usd'],
        row['megapixels'],
        f"  {row['model_year']}\n  {row['sensor_type']}",
        ha='left',
        va='center',
        fontsize=10,
        fontweight='medium'
    )

ax.set_ylabel('Megapixels (MP)', fontsize=14, labelpad=15)

# Format the x-axis to show currency
formatter = mticker.FormatStrFormatter('$%.0f')

plt.xticks(rotation=45)
